a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal

claims.claim: The query is a close linezolid analog sharing the 2-oxazolidinone core and N-aryl morpholine/morpholinone motif; linezolid has measured absolute oral bioavailability of 93.01 ± 23.34% after 600 mg tablets in fasted healthy subjects, is reported as almost 100% bioavailable in fasted healthy volunteers, and the tablet is highly bioavailable relative to IV.

L3 oral exposure records for linezolid show substantial systemic exposure after oral dosing (median Cmax 18.3–18.9 µg/mL at 600 mg daily; mean Cmax 11.9 mg/L in elderly patients; AUCtau 99.2 µg·h/mL after 500 mg multiple dosing), consistent with high oral absorption.

Tedizolid, another oxazolidinone, achieved oral AUC 20.4–26.1 µg·h/mL versus IV 23.5–30.5 µg·h/mL and oral Cmax 2.25 versus IV 3.02 µg/mL after 200 mg phosphate prodrug, indicating oral exposure approximately 75–91% of IV and supporting class-level high oral bioavailability.

L4/L5 permeability records for morpholine-containing small molecules show high Caco-2 permeability with no or low efflux where reported (Papp roughly 21–43 ×10^-6 cm/s; ER 0.55–1.3), weakly supporting favorable intestinal absorption for the query's scaffold, though these records are not query-specific.
No visible record provides affirmative evidence for F <20%; L5 efflux-positive records (C59, C62, C57) are for unrelated scaffolds and do not establish a query-specific gut-wall efflux liability.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule itself.

The query differs from linezolid at the amide substituent (5-chlorothiophene-2-carbonyl vs acetyl), the morpholine ring (3-one vs unsubstituted), and the absence of the aryl fluorine; these changes could affect absorption, solubility, or first-pass metabolism.

No query-specific experimental solubility, permeability, efflux, or metabolic stability data are available; L4/L5 records are for other scaffolds and cannot directly establish query absorption or presystemic loss.
The query's prandial state and formulation are unspecified, while the closest linezolid F values were obtained under fasted conditions with tablets.
L5 gut-wall efflux/intestinal metabolism records are mechanistic and not direct oral-bioavailability results; efflux-positive records are for unrelated scaffolds.
